missions.title: Protect the family: life cover
missions.scoreNote: This is the plan's biggest single score move.

facts.label: Household cover after the plan's move

steps.title: See how far your cover is from the plan's range
steps.body: Each of you has some life cover today, and it sits well below the range the plan recommends for you. If one income stopped, the other person would carry the whole household. Look at your own range, not a share of the household total.

steps.title: Find your current life policy
steps.body: Before you ask for any quote, know exactly what you have now: who the insurer is, how much it pays out and what type of policy it is.
steps.kit: Where to look: a letter or email from the insurer, your employer's benefits portal, or the policy documents in your files. Write down three things: the insurer, the amount, and the type of policy.

steps.title: Ask for a quote inside your recommended range
steps.body: Contact an insurer or an independent agent and ask for a quote for an amount inside your own range. The plan does not name a product or a price, so these quotes are your first real numbers.
steps.kit: What they will usually ask: your age, your health, your income, the amount of cover and how long you want it to last. Compare two or three quotes. For each one, ask what the monthly cost is, what is excluded, and whether the price can change over time.

steps.title: Choose a policy and apply
steps.body: Pick the quote that fits you and send the application. Tap "I did it" when you have applied. That is the checkpoint.

missions.title: Shield what you've built: umbrella cover
missions.scoreNote: It lifts the score a little alone, and more together with life cover.

facts.label: Home and car a claim could reach
Cash and investments a claim could reach

steps.title: See what a large claim could reach
steps.body: Without an umbrella, one large liability claim could reach your home, your car, and the cash and investments you hold. The plan recommends an umbrella policy on top of your home and auto cover.

steps.title: Find your home and auto policies
steps.body: The plan flags your home and your car as not insured. That may only mean details are missing in the data. An umbrella sits on top of those policies, so confirm what you already have.
steps.kit: Where to look: your insurer's app or website, or last year's renewal letters. Write down the insurer and the liability limits on each policy.

steps.title: Ask for an umbrella quote
steps.body: The plan has no price for umbrella cover, so this quote is the first real number you will see.
steps.kit: Start with the insurer that already covers your home and car. Ask for an umbrella quote at the amount the plan recommends. They will usually ask for your current liability limits and for details of your household and vehicles.

steps.title: Sign and put it in place
steps.body: When you are happy with the quote, sign the policy. Tap "I did it" once it is active.

missions.title: Decide together where your free cash flow goes
missions.scoreNote: This is a decision, not a score move. It sets the order of the next missions.

facts.label: Extra retirement saving the plan calls for, per year
Extra college saving needed in the first year

steps.title: See the four needs that share the same money
steps.body: Protection, the cash reserve, retirement saving and the college fund all draw on the same yearly free cash flow, and the mortgage payment has to fit alongside them. The plan says its data does not settle which comes first, so it is your choice.

steps.title: Put the needs in your own order
steps.body: Each of you, on your own, puts the needs in the order you would choose. It is fine if your orders differ: that is the conversation to have next.

steps.title: Agree one order, and optionally an amount for each
steps.body: Compare your orders and agree one. If you like, also decide how much of the yearly free cash flow goes to each need. Any amount you pick is your own number, not the plan's.
steps.kit: Have the plan's facts side by side while you talk: the free cash flow, the cash gap, the retirement need, the card balance and the college need. The plan itself suggests taking small, clear steps rather than everything at once.

missions.title: Build your cushion: cash reserve
missions.scoreNote: It doesn't move the Sherpas score. Its effect shows in your cash numbers.

facts.label: Months of essential expenses it covers
Cash target, from (reserve plus near-term goals)
Vacation payment included in the target (January 2027)

steps.title: See what the cushion is for
steps.body: A cash reserve lets you handle a lost paycheck or a big bill without selling investments at a bad time. Your accessible cash today is far below the plan's target. The plan says closing the gap will take time, so steady progress is the goal.

steps.title: Set up an automatic monthly transfer to savings
steps.body: Choose the monthly amount you agreed in the cash flow decision, and set up a transfer that moves it to savings on its own.
steps.kit: In your bank app, look for "transfers" or "recurring transfers". Pick the source account, the savings account, the amount and a day just after payday. Have at hand: both account names and the amount you agreed.

steps.title: Make the first transfer
steps.body: Confirm the first transfer went through. Later, you can type in your savings balance at check-ins and compare it with the plan's target.

missions.title: Start paying your future selves: retirement saving
missions.scoreNote: On its own it adds a little. With the two protection moves the combined score stays the same.

facts.label: Each of you can contribute per year
Extra saving the plan calls for, per year
Tax it could save per year if both of you contribute in full
HSA: most you could put in per year, if eligible

steps.title: See what goes in today and what could
steps.body: Right now nothing goes into your 401(k)s. Each of you could contribute up to the yearly limit, and the plan calls for more saving than your free cash flow covers today. No employer match is recorded, but the plan flags that as unconfirmed.

steps.title: Ask HR about the match and the HSA
steps.body: Send your HR team one short email. You need two answers: does the company offer a 401(k) match, and does your health plan qualify for an HSA.
steps.kit: Hi, I'd like to start contributing to my 401(k). Could you tell me first whether the company offers a match and how it works, and second whether my health plan is eligible for an HSA? Thanks, {name}.

steps.title: Set your 401(k) contribution
steps.body: In your employer's portal, set the amount you contribute from each paycheck. Use the amount you agreed in the cash flow decision.
steps.kit: It is usually in the benefits or retirement section of the employer portal. Have at hand: your login, the amount you agreed, and the answer from HR about the match.

steps.title: If HR said yes, start your HSA
steps.body: Only do this if HR confirmed your health plan qualifies. The plan calls the HSA a secondary step, to come after the bigger priorities, so it stays last.

missions.title: Tame the credit card
missions.scoreNote: It doesn't move the Sherpas score. It shows in how much interest you pay.

facts.label: Part of each payment that is interest, at today's balance
Paid off at the current payment

steps.title: See what the card costs you
steps.body: This is your costliest debt. A large part of every payment goes to interest, not to the balance. At today's payment the plan shows when it would be paid off.

steps.title: Decide whether a higher payment fits
steps.body: Look at what you agreed in the cash flow decision and decide whether a bigger monthly payment fits. The plan does not compute a new payoff date, so we do not show one.

steps.title: Change the autopay amount
steps.body: The card is Daniel's. Change the automatic payment to the amount you decided.
steps.kit: In the card's app or website, look for "autopay" or "payment settings". Pick a fixed amount and enter the new payment. Have at hand: your login and the amount you decided.

missions.title: College for Oliver and Sophia: the college savings plan
missions.scoreNote: It doesn't move the Sherpas score. It shows in the college funding gap.

facts.label: Extra saving needed in the first year (it rises each year)

steps.title: See where the college fund stands
steps.body: You already save in a college savings plan. The plan shows what is saved, what goes in each year, the gap that remains and when each child starts.

steps.title: Adjust the college savings contribution
steps.body: The college savings plan is Emily's. Change the yearly contribution to the amount you agreed in the cash flow decision.
steps.kit: In the plan's portal, look for "contributions" or "automatic investments". Change the amount and the schedule. Have at hand: your login and the amount you agreed.

missions.title: Invest toward your target mix
missions.scoreNote: It doesn't move the Sherpas score. It shows in how your investments are spread.

facts.label: Plan flag on Daniel's 401(k) mix (Active means worth a look)
Plan flag on Emily's 401(k) mix (None means on target)

steps.title: See your mix next to the plan's target
steps.body: The plan compares the mix of stocks and bonds you hold with the mix it recommends, and shows how both behaved in past markets. Those are past results, not a promise. Emily's 401(k) is on target; Daniel's is the account to look at.

steps.title: Get ready to review the mix with your advisor
steps.body: The report presents this as a proposal to review with your advisor, not an instruction.
steps.kit: Bring to that conversation: the plan's current and target mix, the account statement for your 401(k), and the risk profile you chose.

steps.title: Change the fund mix in your 401(k) portal
steps.body: After the review, change the fund mix in your 401(k) portal to the mix you settled on.

keepInView.title: Your household leans on two paychecks
keepInView.body: Your salaries are a large share of your net worth. The plan says to keep this in view, with no action now. It is one more reason protection comes first.

facts.label: Salaries as a share of net worth

keepInView.title: Long-term care is not planned for
keepInView.body: The plan notes that long-term care costs are not part of the numbers. There is nothing to do now. It is a caveat to remember.
